title: Count cycles in a five-stage pipeline
brief: Model IF, ID, EX, MEM, and WB, find read-after-write hazards, count stalls with and without forwarding, include the load-use bubble, and compute CPI.
hints: With n instructions and no stalls, the last one finishes in n + 4 cycles: the first needs 5, and each later one adds 1. For n = 0 the answer is 0.

find_raw: for consumer j and each source register, walk back from j - 1 to j - 2 and stop at the first instruction whose dest is that register. That nearest writer is the producer. Report (producer, consumer) once per pair.
Without forwarding, model each instruction by the cycle id[i] in which it is in ID. id[0] = 2. A consumer cannot leave ID before its producer's WB cycle, which is id[producer] + 3.

id[i] = max(id[i-1] + 1, id[p] + 3 for each producer p of a source of i). The stalls before instruction i are id[i] - (id[i-1] + 1). The producer p is the latest earlier instruction whose dest is that source.
With forwarding, only a load followed immediately by a user of its result stalls, for exactly one cycle. A load two instructions earlier is already forwarded. An ALU result never stalls.
Total cycles is 0 for an empty program, otherwise len(program) + 4 + sum(stalls). CPI is total cycles divided by instruction count.
The instruction x0 is not a dependency: `parse` already leaves x0 out of dest and srcs, so you never need to special-case it.
